welcome: Welcome to FireFusion AI. This dashboard harmonizes NASA MODIS and VIIRS fire detections for California, July to September 2026. The map shows every detection, coloured by sensor and matching status. The calendar shows daily activity and flags unusual days. The Comparison Lab shows how the matching changes when the distance and time rules change, and how fire radiative power compares between the sensors. Select any day or group and I will describe what the data actually shows. Source: MODIS C6.1 and VIIRS 375 m (NOAA-20, S-NPP), NASA FIRMS, 1 July - 30 September 2026.
sensor_explainer: MODIS and VIIRS see fire differently. MODIS observes at about 1 km resolution from two satellites, Terra in the morning and Aqua in the afternoon, and reports confidence as a number from 0 to 100. VIIRS observes at 375 m from NOAA-20 and S-NPP, and reports confidence as low, nominal or high. Because VIIRS pixels are smaller, it detects more, smaller fires than MODIS, and its fire radiative power values are lower for the same fire -- a 1 km MODIS pixel integrates more burning area than a 375 m VIIRS pixel. That is why the two sensors are compared, never added together. Source: MODIS C6.1 and VIIRS 375 m (NOAA-20, S-NPP), NASA FIRMS, 1 July - 30 September 2026.
season: Across 1 July - 30 September 2026, FireFusion AI harmonized 3318 MODIS detections and 29709 VIIRS detections from California. The harmonization found 64 confirmed one-to-one matched pairs and 418 ambiguous candidate groups; 22274 detections had no cross-sensor partner. The busiest day was 11 August 2026 with 1414 detections. 3 critical periods were identified, when daily activity stayed above the baseline for two or more consecutive days. These are satellite detections, not a count of unique real-world fires. Source: MODIS C6.1 and VIIRS 375 m (NOAA-20, S-NPP), NASA FIRMS, 1 July - 30 September 2026.
